messages:
deploy-bot: rollout complete for service-inference v2026.3 -> canary 10% (eu-west-1 + us-east-1). release notes: https://redwood.internal/releases/v2026.3 :rocket:
alex: noticing a mini-probe spike right after rollout, eu-west-1 postdeploy check 1 failing 3/5 windows, p95 latency ~480ms :eyes:
maria: same. failures look tied to cold-start path hitting model-servers that did not warm KV cache. few 502/504s, not cluster-wide but concentrated on two hosts
sam: can we pause the canary and pin eu-west-1 to previous version until we debug? want to avoid full rollback unless needed
ops-runner: pausing canary and pinning eu-west-1 to v2026.2 now. running: curl -X POST https://ops-api/pin?svc=service-inference&region=eu-west-1&version=v2026.2 :white_check_mark:
deploy-bot: canary paused by policy (automated gate). traffic shifted back to v2026.2 in eu-west-1, continuing 10% in us-east-1
jing: digging into logs, snippet: ```2026-03-10T14:07:11Z ERROR model-server-17 kv-cache lookup timed out=200ms trace=abc123 request_id=...``` repeated pattern on two hosts, GC looked normal
alex: sounds like warmup race. I propose increasing probe hysteresis: require 3 consecutive failing probe-winds before triggering regional rollback, and add a short prefetch warmup on rollout hooks
maria: agree on hysteresis change long-term. short-term: keep the pin and re-run warmup job to repopulate KV for the two affected hosts. ops-runner can you kick warmup?
ops-runner: warmup job queued: jobs/warmup-service-inference/2365011122, started on the two hosts. ETA ~120s
sam: I'll monitor post-warmup synth-checks and escalate if errors persist beyond 10m. opening incident ticket INC-20260310-27 to track
jing: after warmup, quickcheck shows probe success 5/5, p95 back to ~90ms. logs no longer show kv-cache timeouts
deploy-bot: canary resume: re-enabling canary in eu-west-1 at 5% then gradual as per policy
alex: leaving the hysteresis PR on my queue, will add a flag to make it configurable per-service. cc @maria for review
maria: thanks. add a note in release notes about warmup requirement for model-server changes :memo:
